text: A quarter to five, and the man in aisle twenty-two is eating kibble from the bag.
You shine your light on him. He doesn't run. "Hands up. Now."
He puts his hands up slow. "I hid at closing. Nowhere else to go."
Ray. Hood up, staring at the floor. His hands won't stop shaking.
Marcus kicks the fire exit. Snow hisses through the gap. "Every door's buried."
Dana checks the camera log. "Ten fifty-eight. He was inside before I locked up."
"He's been in here all night, watching us," Marcus says. "He's starving," Dana snaps. "Let him eat."
Afternoon. Every freezer alarm in the store starts screaming.
Dana opens a freezer door. "It's soup in here. Warm fog rolling out."
Marcus stares outside. "The drift's colder than any freezer. Move it."
Marcus hauls the bay door up. It stops at one foot of white.
You shove the first pallet of frozen chicken into the drift.
By nightfall the drift is a tunnel of meat.
Day three. Six in the morning. The generator coughs twice and dies.
The lights die one by one. The store goes black.
Dana lifts the fuel can. "It's bone dry. Someone drained it."
"Three days of fuel, gone in two," Marcus says. Dana turns. "Who had the can?"
Four flashlights in the dark. Nobody speaks. Who took three days of fuel?
